card.name: Ballroom dance
card.era: Roots traced to late 16th century (Arbeau's Orchésographie, 1588); modern competitive form early 20th century
card.tagline: Elegant partnered social and competitive dances, from waltz to quickstep.
card.profile: Ballroom dance is a set of European partner dances enjoyed socially and competitively worldwide. Per Encyclopædia Britannica, it is a type of social dancing originally practiced in Europe and the United States, performed by couples following prescribed steps, historically distinguished from folk dance by its association with elite social classes and invitational dance events. With the rise of DanceSport the term narrowed to the dances recognized by two principal schools - the International School (Standard and Latin) and the American School (Smooth and Rhythm) (Wikipedia).
card.insight: Ballroom dance democratized over the 20th century from an aristocratic pastime into a global social and competitive activity, popularized by figures such as Vernon and Irene Castle, Fred Astaire, and Arthur Murray (Encyclopædia Britannica).

parts.note: Introduction to basic elements of ballroom dancing

steps.name: Box Step
steps.description: Forward, side, together, back, side, together

steps.name: Triple Step
steps.description: Three small steps with weight change at the end

steps.name: Rock Step
steps.description: Rocking weight back and forth between feet

common_mistakes: Not changing body weight on the together steps
lessons.teacher_style: The teacher breaks down fundamental ballroom steps using clear verbal instructions and physical demonstrations with a partner. He emphasizes weight changes and styling variations for each basic element.
lessons.distinctive_method: Teaching three universal foundational steps (box step, triple step, rock step) as the building blocks for multiple different ballroom and social dances.
what_works: Demonstrating with a partner helps visualize social dance positioning
Breaking dances down into three core foundational steps
what_hinders: Camera angles shift between front and back views which can require adjustment

evidence.observation: Teacher demonstrates box step holding partner's hand, stepping forward with left foot.
Teacher demonstrates waltz frame hand placement on partner's shoulder blade.

observation.setting: A large ornate ballroom with high vaulted ceilings, arched architectural pillars, chandeliers, and red and blue stage lighting, featuring an orchestra on a side stage.
observation.dancers: A large group of young adults dancing in couples.
observation.formation_and_space: Couples spread across a polished wooden floor, rotating and moving in circular patterns together.
observation.posture: Upright, upright torsos with straight backs and engaged core posture.
observation.footwork: Gliding, light stepping patterns matching a steady waltz rhythm, with rapid rotational steps that make precise foot placement partially occluded.
observation.arms_and_hands: Traditional closed ballroom frame with one hand held outward, some dancers holding red roses.
observation.hips_and_torso: Torsos remain upright and relatively still while turning smoothly with the partner.
observation.partnering: Closed dance hold with one hand linked, leading and following rotational movements.
observation.levels_jumps_turns: Continuous spinning turns across the floor with occasional kneeling poses.
observation.costume_and_props: Men wear black tailcoats, white shirts, and bow ties with white gloves; women wear white floor-length evening gowns with long white gloves and hair accessories or tiaras, some holding red roses.
observation.cannot_infer: Precise individual weight transfer and foot positioning are obscured by long dresses and rapid group movement.

signature_moments.what: Couples perform a synchronized rotational turn with arms extended outward, spinning smoothly across the floor.
